attribution.title: Data & attribution
attribution.intro: This site is built on several open data sources. Their licences require attribution, and crediting them is the right thing to do regardless.
attribution.gbifBody: Seed records come from the <tairon>Taiwan Roadkill Observation Network (TaiRON)</tairon> via <gbif>GBIF</gbif>. These records are licensed CC BY 4.0, which requires attribution.
attribution.taicolBody: Scientific names, Chinese names, taxonomy, protection levels and sensitivity ratings all come from the <taicol>Catalogue of Life in Taiwan (TaiCOL)</taicol>. Our location-blurring rules follow its sensitivity ratings directly.
attribution.basemapBody: The basemap is served by OpenFreeMap, using OpenMapTiles vector tiles built from OpenStreetMap contributors' data (ODbL).
attribution.modelsBody: Species identification uses BioCLIP 2 (MIT) for zero-shot classification and MegaDetector (MIT) for cropping. Candidates are restricted to species on the Taiwan checklist.
attribution.ourDataBody: Reports submitted through this site belong to the people who made them. We intend to publish them back to GBIF as a Darwin Core Archive so the records are usable beyond this site.

about.title: About
about.whatBody: A public map of environmental reports for Taiwan. Anyone can report roadkill, invasive species, pollution or other observations; reports with a photo are passed to an open-source model that attempts to identify the species; everyone can see the aggregated heatmap.
about.privacyBody: Publishing precise coordinates of protected or sensitive species is, functionally, a map for poachers. GBIF, eBird and iNaturalist all obscure such records, and so do we: for those species the public map shows a deliberately coarsened location rather than the real one, and the most sensitive show no coordinates at all.
about.unknownBody: A freshly submitted report is held back and stored at coarse precision until its species is known. Before identification we cannot tell whether it is sensitive — it might be a leopard cat.
about.contributeBody: Just submit a report; no account is needed. Signing in only gives you your own history.
about.contactBody: Questions, corrections, or collaboration — write to Neo Su.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This describes what the site actually collects and does with it. Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act (個人資料保護法) applies.
privacy.collectBody: The coordinates, time, category and notes of a report, plus any photos you upload. An email address is optional, used only to follow up, and is never shown on the map or included in public data. If you sign in we store your account id so your reports can be listed back to you.
privacy.photosBody: Photos are downscaled and stripped of all EXIF metadata — including device model and serial number — in your browser, before they leave your device. If a photo contains GPS data we offer it as a suggested location; it is never applied automatically.
privacy.locationBody: True coordinates are stored in the database only. The public map shows a location adjusted according to the species' sensitivity rating. See the About page for how that works.
privacy.retentionBody: Reports are kept indefinitely, because their scientific value comes from accumulating over time. If you want your report or contact email removed, get in touch.
privacy.thirdPartyBody: The site uses Supabase (database and file storage), Vercel (hosting), OpenFreeMap and OpenStreetMap (basemap), and Modal (AI inference). Photos are sent to the inference service for species identification. Map tiles load from OpenFreeMap through Cloudflare, and OpenFreeMap may log IP addresses for up to 30 days when investigating abuse.
privacy.analyticsBody: We count page views through Vercel Analytics, to see how many people find the reporting page. It sets no cookies, creates no cross-site identifier, and records nothing that identifies a person — what we see is “the home page was viewed N times”, not who viewed it.
privacy.cookiesBody: Only an essential session cookie, and only if you choose to sign in. No advertising or tracking cookies are used.
privacy.contactBody: To ask about, correct, or remove your own reports and contact address — or with any question about how this site handles personal data — write to Neo Su, who is responsible for this site. We will reply within a reasonable time.

statsPage.title: Statistics
statsPage.intro: A summary of every published report. Refreshed every 15 minutes.
statsPage.seasonalityHint: Roadkill is strongly seasonal — amphibians during the spring migration, snakes through the warm months.
statsPage.byYearHint: Changes reflect both what happened and how much surveying was done; the two are hard to separate.
statsPage.topSpeciesHint: Follow a species for its distribution map and details.
statsPage.hotspotsHint: The densest 5km cells and the species that dominates each. Obscured records are excluded so that blurring cannot manufacture a false hotspot. Follow one to see it on the map.
statsPage.coverageBody: Of {total} published records, {obscured} have blurred coordinates because their species is flagged sensitive in TaiCOL. They are still counted in every statistic here; only their mapped position is approximate.
statsPage.seasonLinkHint: A shared target for everyone reporting in Taiwan — reach the squares of the map that have no record at all.

season.title: This season's goal
season.lede: One shared target for everyone reporting in Taiwan: put a first record into {km} km squares of the map that have none at all. Anonymous reports count exactly the same as signed-in ones.
season.noneYet: Nothing new yet this season. A first record from a square that has never had one is the most useful thing anyone can file.
season.progress: Each of these is a square of Taiwan that had no record at all until someone went there.
season.cellsHint: Counted from published records that carry an exact location.
season.speciesHint: TaiCOL lists this many species for Taiwan. Almost none of them have ever been reported here.
season.obscuredNote: {n} published records are left out of the squares above. Their species is rated sensitive, so their location is published coarsely and crediting it to a {km} km square would credit the wrong one. They count in every other statistic on this site.
season.whyBody: A target counted in records rewards volume, and the cheapest volume is the same roadside verge photographed again tomorrow. This one counts only the first record in a {km} km square, so a second is worth nothing and there is no reason to sit on a site you already know. It is also what the data is short of: most records here come from a handful of surveyed roads, which describes those roads rather than the island.
season.noRewardBody: There are no points here, no ranking, and nothing to win. These records are published as open data under this project's name, and attaching a reward to filing one would put a price on getting it wrong.

home.headline: Every life lost on the road deserves a record.
home.sub: Taiwan's roads kill countless wild animals every year. We turn those overlooked deaths into open data — anyone can report, a model helps identify the species, and everyone can see where the hotspots are.
home.mapHint: Tap any cell for its report count
home.whyLede: Roadkill, invasive species, damaged habitats — all of it happens by the roadside every day, and almost none of it is written down systematically.
home.whyRoadkillBody: Roads cut habitat into fragments. Leopard cats, pangolins, crab-eating mongooses — killed under wheels every year, and most are never recorded.
home.whyInvasiveBody: Green iguanas, apple snails, mile-a-minute vine. The earlier the spreading edge is found, the more can be done about it.
home.speciesHeading: Who is dying on the roads?
home.speciesLede: The species reported most often in the public record. Open one to see its distribution, seasonal pattern and conservation status.
home.howHeading: From one photo to one public record
home.how1Body: One photo from the roadside, drop a pin, send. No account needed. EXIF is stripped in the browser before anything is uploaded.
home.how2Body: BioCLIP 2, open source, matched against the Taiwan species checklist. Confident results are assigned; uncertain ones go to a human.
home.how3: It goes on the public map
home.how3Body: Every report feeds a public hotspot map and open statistics. Coordinates of protected and sensitive species are blurred before publication.
home.trustBody: Publishing exact coordinates for a protected species is drawing a map for poachers. Records of sensitive species are published at a deliberately coarse location, following the sensitivity rating in the Taiwan species checklist.
home.openBody: Seeded with records from TaiRON via GBIF (CC BY 4.0), with names from TaiCOL. We plan to contribute our own records back to GBIF as a Darwin Core Archive.
home.finalTitle: If you see one, take a minute.
home.finalBody: One photo, one minute. Your record becomes part of the open scientific record.
